column1: # tools/perf/budgets.tsv — PAGE-BUDGETS: the allowed cost of each page. The only place these numbers live:
# gate.sh (G1 and G9 limits, via budgets.py get) and the morning report (## budgets, budgets.py read) read them here.
# Columns (tab-separated): page, metric, max, basis. page "*" = every page without its own row for that metric.
# Metrics:
#   idle_app_pct  app process CPU while the page is shown and nobody uses the Mac, % of one core (100 = one core busy).
#                 Readings: gate G1 (home) and G9 (cpu) app_pct, sampled with top, no instrument attached; every page
#                 from the MAIN-THREAD-AUDIT Time Profiler recording (includes Time Profiler's own overhead).
#   frame_ms      time of one frame while the page scrolls or animates, with the 144 Hz display as main; the budget
#                 is one refresh interval, so no frame misses its deadline. No night job records it yet (no data).
# Derivation of the "*" idle budget (2026-11-08):
#   1.5   always-on floor: Home's idle cost before SOC-DETAILS (night gate G1 medians 1.58, 1.51, 1.54, 2026-11-04..06)
#   +0.35 one page update per 2 s default sampler tick, each fitting one 144 Hz frame (6.94 ms every 2 s)
#   +1.0  the user's action threshold: about 1 % of one core is no reason for a block (2026-11-03)
#   = 2.85, rounded up to the half percent. Quiet pages share it: their 0.35 less is below the action threshold.
# Sources: Apple, Understanding hitches in your app (a frame shown after its refresh deadline is a hitch),
#   https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xcode/understanding-hitches-in-your-app
#   Apple, Energy Efficiency Guide for Mac Apps (work only when needed, near zero CPU when nothing changes),
#   https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/Performance/Conceptual/power_efficiency_guidelines_osx/
